name: Hu Jintao
role: General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party (2002-2012) and President of China (2003-2013)
summary: Hu Jintao led China as an authoritarian Party leader committed to one-party rule, regional ethnic autonomy under Party leadership, a socialist market economy with a dominant state sector, 'one country, two systems' for Hong Kong and Macao and no tolerance of Taiwan independence, while abroad he stressed development, equal sovereignty, multipolarity, opposition to protectionism and aid for developing countries.

sources.title: Hold High the Great Banner of Socialism with Chinese Characteristics and Strive for New Victories in Building a Moderately Prosperous Society in All Respects: report to the 17th National Congress of the Communist Party of China, 15 October 2007 (USC US-China Institute copy)
sources.author: Hu Jintao
sources.usedFor: The Party's leadership, the political system, ethnic autonomy, the socialist market economy and state sector, one country two systems.

sources.title: Statement by Hu Jintao, President of China, UN General Assembly general debate, 64th session (2009) (UN General Debate Corpus, CHN_64_2009)
sources.author: Hu Jintao; UN General Debate Corpus (Baturo, Dasandi and Mikhaylov), Harvard Dataverse
sources.usedFor: Security, development, protectionism, aid and debt relief, climate, civilizations and the choice of development paths.

sources.title: Hu Jintao in joint press conference with President Bush, Washington, CNN The Situation Room, 20 April 2006 (MediaSum transcript CNN-105161)
sources.author: Hu Jintao
sources.usedFor: His statement that China will never allow anyone to make Taiwan secede by any means.

sources.title: Hu Jintao in joint press conference with Prime Minister Koizumi, CNN Lou Dobbs Tonight, 21 November 2005 (MediaSum transcript CNN-99841)
sources.author: Hu Jintao
sources.usedFor: His statement that China will by no means tolerate so-called Taiwan independence.

sources.title: Anti-Secession Law of the People's Republic of China (2005, Articles 2, 5 and 8), English translation, CSIS Interpret
sources.author: National People's Congress, enacted under President Hu Jintao
sources.usedFor: The state shall never allow Taiwan secession, may employ non-peaceful means if Taiwan secedes or peaceful reunification is exhausted, and Taiwan may practise different systems after peaceful reunification.

sources.title: Firmly March on the Path of Socialism with Chinese Characteristics and Strive to Complete the Building of a Moderately Prosperous Society in All Respects: report to the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China, 8 November 2012 (Xinhua text, Chinese Embassy in the US)
sources.author: Hu Jintao
sources.usedFor: The socialist system with Chinese characteristics: people's congresses, multiparty cooperation under CPC leadership, ethnic autonomy, public ownership as the mainstay.

sources.title: Letter from the Consortium for Liu Xiaobo to NPC Chairman Wu Bangguo, Human Rights Watch (2010)
sources.author: Human Rights Watch and signatories
sources.usedFor: Liu Xiaobo sentenced on 25 December 2009 to 11 years for inciting subversion over six internet essays criticising Communist Party rule.

sources.title: "I Saw It with My Own Eyes": Abuses by Chinese Security Forces in Tibet, 2008-2010, Human Rights Watch (July 2010)
sources.author: Human Rights Watch
sources.usedFor: Disproportionate force, shootings, detentions and sentences after the 2008 Tibetan protests, and the government's refusal of independent investigation.

sources.title: "We Are Afraid to Even Look for Them": Enforced Disappearances in the Wake of Xinjiang's Protests, Human Rights Watch (October 2009)

notes: First audit. Read the 2007 Party Congress report by theme (Party leadership, democracy and the legal system, ethnic autonomy, the economy, the armed forces, Taiwan and Hong Kong) and his 2009 address to the UN General Assembly in the local corpus; the MediaSum press-conference quotes are cited for Taiwan. In MediaSum he says that without democracy there is no modernization and that China will protect freedom, democracy and human rights according to law, and that much remains to be done on human rights; these state no position on the test's democracy statements (the Party leads) and stay null. Acts under him are cited from the 2005 Anti-Secession Law, the Liu Xiaobo sentence, the 2009 Urumqi disappearances and the 2008 Tibet crackdown (Human Rights Watch reports) and the 2007 Labor Contract Law (law-firm summary); the 2006 abolition of the agricultural tax and his 1989 Lhasa martial-law role were not found in an open source. The 2012 report was read for the political and economic system.
